findings.message: F1 (assessment, Bloom tag): the Urdu ERQ-2 question is tagged *(جانچنا)* (Evaluate) where the accepted English ERQ-2 is tagged *(Analyze)* (docs/semester-1/gict-300/unit-05/unit-assessment.mdx line 132, repaired at a7200d2 and verified by G3 run 002 finding F4). Locator: i18n/ur/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current/semester-1/gict-300/unit-05/unit-assessment.mdx line 129 (ERQ-2 tag). The Urdu file is internally inconsistent - its own ERQ-2 rubric heading (line 197) says (تجزیہ) (Analyze) - and the a7200d2 commit message claims the tag was aligned "EN + UR", but the Urdu question tag was created with the pre-repair value. A teacher or student working from the Urdu sees the item's declared cognitive demand as Evaluate, diverging from the accepted English item; no deterministic gate covers Urdu Bloom tags (check-bloom-bands reads English tags only), so only G5 review catches it. Systematic comparison of all 25 assessment Bloom tags confirms this is the sole mismatch. Repair request: change جانچنا to تجزیہ in the ERQ-2 question tag (one word), leaving everything else untouched.

F2 (semantics, quotation boundary): in the fair-use definition the Urdu places "مخصوص صورتوں میں" (in specific cases) INSIDE the quotation marks (i18n topic-03.mdx lines 54-56: "کاپی رائٹ قانون کی وہ حد جو مخصوص صورتوں میں محفوظ کام کے استعمال کی پہلے اجازت کے بغیر اجازت دیتی ہے") while the English keeps "in specific cases, classroom distribution among them" outside the quoted span (docs topic-03.mdx lines 56-59). The bound source's verbatim definition ends at "without prior authorization" (specs/content/gict-300/sources/texts/bourgeois2019.md, Chapter 12 excerpt). The propositional content conveyed to the learner is unchanged and the citation is retained, so this is advisory; but the Urdu attributes a slightly longer span to Bourgeois et al. than the source verbatimly supports. Repair request: move "مخصوص صورتوں میں" outside the closing quotation mark.

F3 (register minors, none meaning-changing): (a) RRQ-6 model answer renders "negligible market effect" as "نظر انداز برابر منڈی اثر" (i18n unit-assessment.mdx line 173-174), a compressed collocation that reads awkwardly (natural: ناہمی / نظر انداز کرنے کے قابل منڈی اثر); context (the four-factor list) recovers the meaning. (b) teacher-notes "رپورٹ ہوا" for "reported" (line 72; more natural رپورٹ شدہ). (c) teacher-notes flattens "presented as if to the Class 7 it was written for" to "اسی جماعت ہفتم کے سامنے پیش کیا جا سکتا ہے جس کے لیے لکھا گیا تھا" (line 73-74) - the as-if framing is slightly reduced. (d) RRQ-2 model answer uses the colloquial adjectival "ذلتی" for "humiliation" (line 161; more formal ذلت). (e) ERQ-5 renders "compliance" as "مطابقت" (lines 135, 207), which leans toward "conformity/compatibility"; the rights-and-responsibilities context disambiguates toward rule-following. None of these reverses or materially shifts meaning.

F4 (terminology, governance table only, not learner-facing): two concept labels in specs/content/gict-300/concepts/unit-05.md carry grammar slips to fix when the labels are promoted into the terminology bank (the file's own G5-flag list): CON:GICT-300-5-6 "بھیجے پیغام کی دوام" (دوام is masculine; expect بھیجے ہوئے پیغام کا دوام) and CON:GICT-300-5-13 "ٹیکنالوجی رسائی بطور سرقے کا سبب" (بطور + کا سبب construction clash; more natural: سرقے کا سبب بننے والی ٹیکنالوجی رسائی). The learner-facing prose and figures do not reuse these exact phrases, so no learner sees the slips.
